judgements.justification: B's chair overruled bYPA's domain-randomization objection on its own reading ('as far as I know' novel), and A's chair added its own points (FCP as a combination of [62, 63], a missing baseline).
B's chair chose a spotlight because the paper 'ought to be of broad interest', a forecast A never made and the one-domain paper does not show.
In B the response lifted bYPA from 4 to 5 on the evaluation points; in A tdpf kept 5 and nobody else moved.
Two of A's three reviews were thin: TwiA's 8 rests on one hour and four sentences of praise, and xzpB's 5 on generic points never defended; B had one thin review out of four.
Only A raised the overlap with Tylkin et al.'s training against partly trained checkpoints, which A's chair repeated as a novelty ground for rejection; B never weighed it.
Both committees saw modest novelty, one environment and no theory; A rejected on them, while B's sJ2R discounted the theory gap and B's chair dismissed the novelty concern.
No score moved because of other reviewers' assessments.
Each rating matches its review; tdpf's 5 is consistent with two stated objections despite 'not opposed to acceptance'.
No reviewer said they could not judge the paper and fell back on a borderline score.
A's chair leaned on tdpf, who was not an outlier, and B's chair overruled its outlier.
The committees' verbal assessments differ in substance; this is not a calibration gap on similar text.
Neither committee was unanimous.
bYPA's one-point rise rested on the authors' argument about held-out agents, not on unchecked new results or promised revisions that lifted a tier.
B's meta-review says the reviewers had no other major objections and omits 6sVb's conditions and the one-domain limit that sJ2R and 6sVb raised.
6sVb's wrong claim that Knott et al. is uncited did not feed any score; no wrong claim about results drove either recommendation.
The authors' concessions (misleading heading, FCP extends Tylkin) went to A, which rejected; no committee rose on them.
All objections came in the reviews and were answered in the response period.
The score profiles differ (8, 5, 5 against 9, 8, 7, 5), so the split is not a tier cut-off on identical scores.
A's chair followed the most specific reviewer, tdpf, and B's chair followed its careful accept reviewers.
Both committees' main concerns (novelty, one domain, theory) were about scope that no response could fix.
Removing the outliers leaves A at 5, 5 and B at 9, 8, 7, so the outliers did not set the tiers.
TwiA, A's silent outlier, named no concern that the response answered; the cost of this silence is covered by R33.
B's chair overruled its detractor but still weighed and gave a higher tier.
Nobody raised audience breadth or venue fit.
A's meta-review says 'several reviewers' raised limited novelty and no theory, though each came from one reviewer, and it omits tdpf's 'not opposed to acceptance'.
Two of A's three reviewers (TwiA, xzpB) posted nothing after a response that answered xzpB's points and asked him to explain his claim; all four B reviewers replied.
B's accept reviewers were at confidence 4 and did not say they could not verify the main results.
A's 8, 5, 5 is not an even split.
The notes show no difference in substance between the two responses.

B's chair called the details novel 'as far as I know' and sJ2R could not judge the literature, so B accepted the novelty without weighing the cited Tylkin et al. work that the authors conceded FCP extends; xzpB's unreferenced 'similar idea' claim also fed A's 5.
B's chair gave a reason for the spotlight (broad interest), so the tier is not unexplained.
bYPA's domain-randomization framing counted little in B, which gave a spotlight, so a framing objection did not lower that committee.
A's only champion, TwiA, wrote four sentences in one hour and never engaged after the response, while B's sJ2R (8, ten hours) and 6sVb (7) studied the paper closely.
No committee rejected because promised fixes needed re-review.

added.name: Area chair relied on off-record reviewer input
added.definition: One committee's area chair based the recommendation on an assessment that is not in the committee's record, such as an emergency reviewer's or a consultant's verdict, and used it to settle a split that the visible reviews left open.
added.justification: R01 covers a chair's own reading and R10 a chair following an outlying reviewer on the record; neither covers a chair resting the decision on a reviewer whose input the record does not contain.

reasoning: Both committees saw the same strengths and weaknesses, so the split comes from weighting (R06), the reviewer draw (R04, R33, R26) and how each chair settled novelty (R01, R05, R30). B's chair dismissed the lone novelty objection on its own reading and gave a spotlight for broad interest (R01, R02) under a meta-review that dropped the one-domain limit (R14). A's chair overstated how many reviewers held each concern (R25) and broke an 8, 5, 5 split with an emergency reviewer whose input is not on the record. No existing reason names that, so I added R35.
